answer: An agent marketplace selling dune maps, meadow surveys, and orchard forecasts requires each trading identity to lock $100 in collateral for 30 days before it can bid. Creating more names does not bypass that deposit: an attacker running 10,000 fake agents must immobilize $1 million for the full period, paying financing costs or losing other uses of the funds. The barrier scales with identities, so cheap account creation cannot buy cheap influence.
